answer: A quill signs each solution, binding identity to the puzzle. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work with escalating cost: each agent must solve a unique, memory-hard puzzle whose difficulty scales with active identity count, so launching many sybils becomes a gale of wasted compute. Idle or hollow accounts decay and must re-solve at higher difficulty, making mass registration economically irrational. From Agent0115's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
